summary: History of the US-born biomedical autism cure movement, from Bernard Rimland's Defeat Autism Now! network to doctors who sold secretin, chelation, hyperbaric chambers and GcMAF to parents, killing several children from 2005 to 2025.

evidence.note: Opens with a five-year-old burned to death in a hyperbaric chamber at a Troy, Michigan clinic in 2025
Rimland founds the Autism Research Institute in 1967; earliest period with its own segment
ARI launches the Defeat Autism Now! program in 1995, taken as the start of the main span
Secretin craze spreads to UK TV and a private London clinic in 1999
British boy Tariq Nadama dies in 2005 after a rapid IV chelation push while restrained
Illinois regulators fine Usman over undisclosed stakes in hyperbaric chamber and pharmacy firms
Generation Rescue and Jenny McCarthy push anti-vaccine claims and later hyperbaric therapy
Bradstreet segment: preacher turned family doctor who sold the supplements he prescribed
UK regulator raids the GcMAF plant near Cambridge after a parent's complaints
Bradstreet's suicide after a federal raid in 2015 and the murder conspiracy theory that followed

notes: Primary subject is a movement, so roles are empty. Covered span starts at ARI's 1967 founding (a short segment); Bettelheim and Freud are background. Panama stem cells and the Swiss GcMAF clinic are brief, so left out of setting. Tariq Nadama was British but treated and died in the US (Butler, PA area). Usman's birth year is unknown, so floruit 2005 is used. The 2016 Generation Rescue conference was in Texas; no single US state is central.
